solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Excellent physical education: hurting all over?

parts.note: PE is the school abbreviation for physical education
achy describes a body that aches throughout

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a punishing gym lesson, leaving them sore everywhere, was really so excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark fits the surface irony; the answer is informal British English for very good.
explanation.definitionFit: Peachy is an informal adjective meaning fine or splendid, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Money for retiree in French boarding house

definitions.meaning: first meaning: regular income paid after retirement
second meaning: a guesthouse in France or elsewhere in Europe

explanation.surface: A pensioner's income is spent lodging in a guesthouse in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a retirement income and, borrowed from French, a small residential hotel.

clue.text: A Liberal frequently high

parts.note: taken as written
oft is an old word meaning often

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is often intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft means up in the air, so high above the ground.

clue.text: Minute distance this bear had moved across river

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so the rearranged letters straddle the river letter
letters that are moved are shifted into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A bear relocates over a stream by only a tiny margin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairsbreadth is a tiny margin, as narrow as the thickness of one strand.

clue.text: Chap requiring some oxygen, temporarily

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these two words are used, a run spanning the word break

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A man needs extra oxygen for a short while, perhaps after exertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Gent is short for gentleman, an informal synonym for a man or fellow.

clue.text: Head away from most dangerous mountain

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which goes away here

parts.note: severest means the most serious or perilous

explanation.surface: A climber is urged to turn away from the most treacherous peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest peak, in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Quality and skill rising with it

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: art can mean a skill or knack
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's character and ability improve along with the thing in question.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing characteristic of a person, a synonym of quality.

clue.text: Which individual gets a command to stop?

parts.note: who asks which person
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which person receives an order to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the call used to bring a horse to a halt, so it is an order to stop.

clue.text: The final section of the histogram changed

indicators.note: letters that are changed are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The last part of a bar chart has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final section' reads as part of the chart, but it is the last stretch of a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The home straight is the last stretch of a race track before the finish, and by extension any closing stage.

clue.text: Nilote worked with hard, stone tool

indicators.note: letters that are worked are shaped into a new form, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A member of a Nile valley people shapes a stone implement with firm, hard strokes.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nilote is a member of a group of peoples from the Nile valley; H is the pencil abbreviation for hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A neolith is a polished stone implement of the New Stone Age, an archaeological term.

clue.text: Greek letter is nothing fantastic

parts.note: O is the round zero standing for nothing
mega is slang for great or fantastic

explanation.surface: Someone declares a letter of the Greek alphabet to be quite unremarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Lacking will, hitch-hiker finally abandons US highway

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so this letter drops out of the highway

parts.note: an interstate is a major American highway linking states

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: only its closing letter is used

explanation.surface: A reluctant hitch-hiker finally gives up on thumbing rides along an American interstate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' reads as determination in the surface, but it is a legal document here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dies intestate has made no valid testament, so their estate passes by the law's default rules.

clue.text: Have beef perhaps, but no starter

indicators.note: a starter is a first course, so the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: beef is one example of meat, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A diner opts for a beef main course but skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' suggests a menu course, but here it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a meal is to consume it, so have and eat are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: No attempt to catch a solicitor

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: catching something means holding it, so this letter goes inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer makes no effort to apprehend anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a notary is a type of solicitor authorised to witness and certify documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary public is a lawyer who certifies documents, a specialised kind of legal practitioner.

clue.text: Enormous bird — a kind with no tail

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
taken as written

indicators.note: a word's tail is its last letter, which is missing here

parts.note: nice can mean kind or pleasant

explanation.surface: A huge bird of a gentle sort that has lost its tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, like the Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: Information about university rank

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the data word goes around the letter for university

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, are numerical information

explanation.surface: Data on a university's position in a league table.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or position in a hierarchy, a synonym of rank.

clue.text: Stay loyal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood from a wound
second meaning: firmly committed and faithful

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an instruction to remain faithful; the verb sense is stopping a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for stemming a flow and an adjective for steadfast devotion.

clue.text: Ancho that's somewhat spicy

indicators.note: somewhat means partly, so only part of these words supplies the answer

parts.note: the answer straddles the end of the pepper's name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: An ancho, a dried Mexican chilli pepper, that has a mild kick.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot food is spicy and pungent, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Useful tips taken from hypnotherapy?

explanation.surface: A patient wonders whether hypnotherapy yields helpful advice.
explanation.walkthrough: The tips of the long word are H and Y, read as the phrase H and Y; the question mark flags this playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Handy means convenient or practical, a synonym of useful.

clue.text: Female — one leaving an Egyptian city

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so the numeral letter is taken out of the city

parts.note: Alexandria is the Mediterranean port founded by Alexander the Great
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman departs from a city in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandra is a woman's given name, and crosswords often define names by gender.

clue.text: Fish drift off, mostly upside down!

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down means the letters are read bottom to top
mostly means nearly all, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: to drift off is to fall asleep

explanation.surface: Fish doze off, most of them floating belly-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long, snake-like fish.

clue.text: Opted to switch bank

indicators.note: to switch is to swap around, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone chose to move their account to a different bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests a financial institution, but here it is a store or stockpile.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse where supplies are kept, as a bank holds reserves.

clue.text: Piece of music is not a soul track primarily

parts.note: not a soul means nobody at all

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A record reviewer insists a song is not a soul number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soul' suggests the music genre, but 'not a soul' is a phrase meaning nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a composition for nine performers, so it is a musical work.

clue.text: Type of ball — extremely large — pings around

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters are used

parts.note: only its two end letters are used

indicators.note: around signals the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A very big ball bounces about with a series of pinging sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg spin is a cricket bowling style in which the ball turns from the leg side towards the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg spin describes a kind of delivery in cricket, so a ball bowled that way is a type.

clue.text: Chuck out every other bit of your cake, it's gross!

indicators.text: Chuck out every other bit of
indicators.note: throwing away every second letter leaves the alternating ones, starting from the first

parts.note: keeping the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone tells a host to bin half of their cake because it tastes disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuck is an interjection expressing disgust, the cry when something is revolting.

clue.text: Small, small person is a pain

parts.note: titch is British slang for a very small person

explanation.surface: A tiny, irritating individual is described as an annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: Titch is a British nickname for a short person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp pain in the side, often felt when running.
